figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. A domain distribution and substrates they accept based on characterized NRP structures. (a) The 4,100 A domains sorted by taxonomic
origin. (b) The A domains sorted by each substrate. Proteinogenic amino acids and selected nonproteinogenic amino acids are listed with their
taxonomic origin. Nomenclature and structures of nonproteinogenic amino acids are provided in Table S1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Sequence-to-substrate correlation of NRPS A domains. (a) Sequence logo analyses of all 4,100 A domains and threonine- or cysteine-
accepting A domains. The A3 to A6 motif area covering the flavodoxin-like subdomain is shown, with substrate-specific conserved residues labeled
by diamonds. See Figure S1 for full-length A domain analysis. (b) Phylogenetic analysis of the flavodoxin-like subdomain, colored by substrates
they accept in the background and by taxonomic origin on the outer strips. See Figure S2 for bootstrap information and Figure S3 for clearer
substrate distribution.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Evaluation of NRPStransformer prediction accuracy. (a) Data set for NRPStransformer development. (b) Benchmarking of
NRPStransformer and other methods against the 763 test data comprising the 43 amino acids. Stachelhaus code and Retrained NRPSpredictor2
used the 3043 training data for algorithm development. PARAS and DeepAden were directly evaluated by running their program to see whether the
outputs matched the test data labels or not. NRPStransformer-Clade prediction was evaluated by the same data set but using the 17 clades as the
data labels. (c) Confusion matrix of NRPStransformer with recall (accuracy) and support (sample) numbers. (d) Violin plot showing each test
sequence and its prediction score of NRPStransformer. (e) Real-world accuracy comparison using the recently published NRPS data. The data set
has not been used to train any of the algorithms and includes rare nonproteinogenic amino acids without any filtering.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Characterization of NRPs guided by NRPStransformer prediction. Asterisks indicate compounds characterized by mass spectrometry in
this study, with red and blue indicating novel and reported compounds, respectively. (a) Discovery of peptides from A. muelleri LMG 22569.
Muelleripeptin A was identified as a major product from fermentation extract by HPLC analysis at UV = 190 nm. (b) Discovery of peptides from C.
rhizoryzae JP2−74. Sch 20561 and its derivatives were discovered by the extracted ion chromatogram (EIC) using the mass of decarboxylated
threonine. (c) Discovery of peptides from S. cattleya NRRL8057. Cattleyapeptins were discovered as major products by HPLC analysis (Figure S5),
and three compounds were observed by EIC of its characteristic 4-methoxytryptophan-derived mass fragment.
